I reconstructed all nine 2,000-term quotient prefixes independently from their polynomials using 5,000-digit Decimal arithmetic, then certified 2,017-digit prefixes by exact rational continued-fraction cylinder endpoints: each cylinder lies inside the stated root-selector interval and the defining polynomial has opposite exact integer signs at its endpoints. On the selector intervals the chosen root is unique (positive-monotone quadratics, one-real-root cubics, and monotone rho9 above 1). All 18,000 stored theta intervals enclose the rational bounds derived from 16-digit certified tail cylinders and q_{k−1}/q_k. Recomputed the 11-bin counts, L1, chi-square, B maxima and unique phi B=1 extremal with zero material discrepancies. The originally claimed generator/verifier scripts are absent from this accepted package; the audit's independent exact-cylinder proof supplies a separate check, but no generator is being represented as committed.

originality.evidence: PASS, scoped to cubic data. Quadratic periods and the golden-ratio B=1 extremum are classical, and OEIS already lists a long cube-root-of-two quotient prefix. Sibbertsen et al. frame degree>2 Gauss–Kuzmin uncertainty but do not provide these nine named exact 2,000-term vectors with the joint discrepancy/theta table. Originality rests on the finite cubic data and combined statistics, not a claim of Gauss–Kuzmin convergence.

scientific_value.evidence: PASS, bounded. The five cubic vectors and their exactly checked finite discrepancy statistics give reproducible test instances for an open metric-number-theory question. A 2,000-term fit neither proves limiting normality nor bounded or unbounded quotients.
